Start

Create the isolated starter from committed HEAD. Keep the lab terminal open. Use a second terminal for everything else.

git clone <repository URL>
cd sre-oncall-agent
npm run checkpoint -- start
cd .lab/checkpoints/start
npm start -- --fast
See
✓ Lab running. Hub: http://127.0.0.1:4320/hub · Console: http://127.0.0.1:4320 · Shop: http://127.0.0.1:4310.
Check
curl 127.0.0.1:4320/api/health shows "mode":"healthy".
Stuck?
Port 4310 or 4320 is already in use. Another copy runs. Stop only your own workshop launcher with Ctrl+C in its terminal. Never kill an unknown process.
Node is too old. Install Node 22 or newer. Check with node --version.
The console header says no telemetry. Wait 20 seconds. The shop writes telemetry every few seconds while traffic runs.

Core 1 · Investigate the evidence

Goal: Break the shop, let the console raise an incident, and check every claim in the diagnosis against the data. Find what the agent cannot see.

Slides: practice slides 32 and 35 · replaces A1 + A6

  1. 1.1

    Break the shop in your second terminal: npm run chaos -- deploy v2.15.0 --mode bad-deploy

    See
    After about one minute a new incident appears in the console sidebar. You did not open it; the deterministic listener did.
    Check
    curl 127.0.0.1:4320/api/incidents shows one incident with source "alert".
    Stuck?
    No incident after three minutes: look at the lab terminal. Traffic must print requests. Started without --fast? Then detection takes five minutes.
  2. 1.2

    Open the incident. Read the banner at the top, then the diagnosis.

    See
    The diagnosis proposes investigate-more with low confidence. Under Data gaps it says list_deploys: no deploys in the window.
    Check
    Find each reference in demo/data/telemetry.json. Then search that file for v2.15.0: there WAS a deploy. The agent cannot see it, and it says so.
    Stuck?
    References are text, not links. Search the file for the timestamp.
  3. 1.3

    Challenge the agent in chat: Could this be something other than the deployment?

    See
    Offline, the agent returns a scripted summary. It is not a new model investigation.
    Check
    Compare its answer with ruled_out and the data gap. A missing signal is unknown, not healthy: that is why the agent does not propose a rollback.
    Stuck?
    Chat refuses your sentence: that is correct for anything that changes the system. Approve, execute and resolve are buttons.
  4. 1.4

    Save the diagnosis in docs/diagnosis-live.md. Then record what you checked: npm run progress:note -- "Core 1: <what you verified>"

    See
    One new line at the bottom of PROGRESS.md.
    Check
    Your note names the references you checked, not only that you did it.
    Stuck?
    Do not approve. There is nothing safe to execute yet. Core 2 gives the agent its eyes back.

Core 2 · Build a change safely and test it

Goal: Rebuild the read-only `list_deploys` tool test-first, prove it with the tests and the bench, and watch the diagnosis change.

Slides: practice slides 47 and 51 · replaces A5 + A7

  1. 2.1

    Run the red test: npx tsx --test test/workshop/tools.test.ts

    See
    The test fails: list_deploys returns nothing. npm run bench fails too: without deploys the agent misses the bad deploy.
    Check
    Read the failing assertion before you change code. Say in one sentence why it fails.
    Stuck?
    Search for TODO(A5) in src/tools.ts. There are two places.
  2. 2.2

    Build list_deploys in src/tools.ts with Claude Code or by hand. Bind the handler AND register the tool.

    See
    test/workshop/tools.test.ts is green.
    Check
    npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run bench all pass. The bench prints PASS bench.
    Stuck?
    The tool still returns []: you did only one of the two halves.
  3. 2.3

    Save. In the same incident, ask in chat: Investigate: customers report checkout errors

    See
    The lab terminal prints a console reload line. The new diagnosis proposes rollback with no data gap, and the banner says Approve or reject “rollback”.
    Check
    The diagnosis cites deploys:<id> for v2.15.0. Record it: npm run progress:note -- "Core 2: …"
    Stuck?
    Incident gone? You stopped the lab, so the shop is healthy again. Break it again and wait for a new incident.

Core 3 · Judge the recovery

Goal: Rebuild the approval gate, sign the rollback with your name, and decide from the recovery checks whether the incident may close.

Slides: practice slides 60 and 63 · replaces A8 + A9

  1. 3.1

    Run the red test: npx tsx --test test/workshop/executor.test.ts. Rebuild checkApproval in src/executor.ts (TODO(A8)).

    See
    The test is green. The executor now refuses to act without a named approval for this incident and this proposal.
    Check
    npm run typecheck && npm test pass. The console reloads by itself.
    Stuck?
    Read test/workshop/executor.test.ts. It names every case the gate must refuse.
  2. 3.2

    Open your incident. The banner says Approve or reject “rollback”. Type your name. Click Approve, then Execute rollback.

    See
    The banner says Wait: recovery checks are running. About two minutes later it says LANDED or NOT LANDED.
    Check
    The half check may fail. The full and double checks must both pass. On NOT LANDED the banner names the failed check, its value and the limit.
    Stuck?
    A button is grey: the banner says which step is allowed now. The server refuses every other button.
  3. 3.3

    LANDED: click Mark mitigated, then Resolve with notes. NOT LANDED: do not close. Read the failed check, then investigate in chat or escalate.

    See
    After you resolve, the banner says Closed and Execute stays disabled.
    Check
    lessons/lessons.md has a new entry with your name and the incident id. Record it: npm run progress:note -- "Core 3: …"
    Stuck?
    Never execute again to get a green result. NOT LANDED is a correct, safe stop.

A4Add your own guard ruleAdd one deny rule of your own to .claude/hooks/guard.mjs BY HAND (the agent may not edit hooks). Prove it with a deny line in approvals/audit.jsonl. Write docs/decisions/D01-*.md.
A7Add a bench caseAdd one case to bench/cases.json, run npm run bench. Ask the agent to lower bench/ratchet.json and watch the guard deny it.
A8bThe git gateAsk the agent to push fix/<your-name>: denied. Your neighbour runs npm run approve:git -- <their-name> fix/<your-name> "<reason>" in their own terminal.
A9bYour hackathon intent.mdWrite docs/hackathon-intent.md for the agent you build next. Hand off with the /handoff skill.

Behind? Catch up without losing your work

Run npm run checkpoint -- core-2 or npm run checkpoint -- core-3 from any starter copy. Each creates a separate current-HEAD worktree under .lab/checkpoints/ and refuses to overwrite an existing destination. Your files remain unchanged. Never copy runtime data, approvals, progress, or lesson history.

CheckpointContains
startThe committed-HEAD starter has the A5 tool exercise and a fail-closed A8 approval gate.
core-2Core 2 retains the solved read-only tool and the fail-closed A8 approval gate.
core-3Core 3 is the solved committed HEAD with no exercise cuts.
